Chapter 9: Humility—The Quiet Strength.
As Hafid’s reputation started to grow, so did the temptation to let pride sneak in.
Then, another scroll arrived—a gentle reminder that real greatness is always rooted in humility.
It’s so easy to start believing that success means you’re somehow better than everyone else. But the scroll made it clear: every person matters, no matter what they’ve achieved.
Pride can be sneaky. It blinds us to our own mistakes and keeps us from learning and growing. Hafid thought back to times when he brushed off others’ advice, certain that he already knew best. Looking back, he realized how that attitude had closed doors and even strained relationships.
One day, a new merchant showed up at the marketplace. He was eager, but still finding his way. While others laughed at his early missteps, Hafid did something different. He reached out, not as someone above him, but as a fellow traveler on the same journey. He shared what he’d learned. And you know what? The young merchant flourished. Hafid felt this quiet satisfaction—not from praise or reward, but from simply helping someone else.
That’s when it really hit him: humility isn’t about thinking less of yourself. It’s about thinking of yourself less.
Most of us get so wrapped up in our own needs and dreams, we forget how much we can help others. The scroll encouraged Hafid to listen more than he spoke, to try to understand before offering advice, and to celebrate other people’s wins just as much as his own.
Over time, Hafid saw that humility opened doors pride would have slammed shut. People started sharing knowledge, working together, and cheering each other on. The marketplace wasn’t just a competition anymore—it became a real community.
So, what’s the real takeaway here?
Let go of the need to always be right, to be recognized, or to outshine everyone else. Focus on serving others, stay curious, and learn from everyone you meet. When you do, life becomes richer—not just with success, but with genuine connection to the people around you.
